Mast Cell Stabilizers (Cromolyn Sodium & Ketotifen): Mechanism of Action & Therapeutic Uses

Agents

  • Cromolyn sodium
  • Ketotifen

Mechanism of action

  • Cromolyn sodium is a mast cell stabilizer that inhibit mast cell degranulation => prevents release of inflammatory mediators including histamine and leukotrienes which cause allergic symptoms and bronchoconstriction
  • Ketotifen is an antihistamine and a mast cell stabilizer, it works by blocking histamine H1 receptors => less allergic symptoms; it also work as to prevent mast cell degranulation and inhibits release of inflammatory mediators (e.g. leukotrienes and histamine)

Pharmacokinetics

  • Cromolyn sodium is available as oral solution, nasal spray, ophthalmic solution, and inhalation solution
  • Cromolyn Oral absorption is really poor, bioavailability is around 0.5- 2% and the majority of the medication (98%) excreted unchanged in the feces
  • Ketotifen is available is oral tablets/solution and ophthalmic solution

Therapeutic uses

Cromolyn sodium is FDA approved for these therapeutic uses:

  • Prophylaxis of bronchial asthma attacks given as metered dose inhaler and nebulizer
  • Adjuvant treatment of allergic rhinitis given as intranasal
  • Systemic mast cell disease (mastocytosis) in pediatric and adult patients (oral solution)
  • Oral Cromolyn sodium solution is used to improve symptoms of diarrhea, flushing, headaches, vomiting, urticaria, abdominal pain and itching
  • Ophthalmic solution for treatment of allergic eye conditions (e.g. keratitis)
  • Cromolyn off label uses include prevention of serious reactions to foods and in management of IBD
  • Ketotifen in its oral form is FDA approved to prevent asthma attacks or anaphylaxis as well as preventing other allergic disorders
  • Ketotifen in its ophthalmic form is used to treat allergic conjunctivitis

Adverse effects

Cromolyn sodium is irritant material that caused local side effects depending on the site of administration:

  • Inhalational route: hoarseness, esophagitis, laryngeal and pharyngeal edema, bronchial irritation, cough and pulmonary infiltrates
  • Intranasal route: nasal congestion, sneezing, nasal itching, nosebleeds and headaches
  • Ophthalmic solution: eye dryness, itchiness and puffiness
  • Cromolyn oral solution may lead to: headache, diarrhea, pruritus, nausea, myalgia, abdominal pain, vomiting, urticaria, angioedema
  • Ketotifen oral route side effects: drowsiness, weight gain, dry mouth, irritability, nosebleeds, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headaches and fatigue; it may also lead to anaphylaxis, liver dysfunction, blood disorders and seizure disorders
  • Ketotifen eye drops may lead to eye redness, eye swelling, eye itching, pain and eye discomfort

Contraindications

  • Both medications are contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity reactions to them

Overdose

  • Ketotifen overdose: sedation, confusion, disorientation, agitation, hallucinations, ataxia, tremor, myoclonus, nystagmus, dysarthria and slurred speech, tachycardia, hypotension, cardiac arrest, pulmonary edema, pancreatitis, hepatitis
  • Overdose is rare with Cromolyn sodium because of the low bioavailability
